title: Clopen alpha projections commute with pasting and pullback before derivation
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For every scheme $X$ use its small pro-etale site with the chosen small skeleton, its constant ring sheaf $\underline B_X$, the abelian category of module sheaves, and $\mathcal T_X=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B_X))$ of strict inverse systems. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal T_X)$. Use the termwise inverse image $G_u$, total derived termwise direct image $R_u$, and exact open extension $J_j$ with their specified adjunctions and compositors [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations] [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Let $Q$ be a commutative square of schemes with $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ quasi-compact open immersions, $r:V\to S$, $p:W\to T$ proper, and $pk=ir$. Put $W_S=W\times_T S$ with projections $b:W_S\to W$, $q:W_S\to S$, and $s=(k,r):V\to W_S$. For each such square take the clopen component projector and the open-unit-normalized cartesian comparison and form $\alpha_Q:G_pJ_i\to J_kG_r$ by the intrinsic construction [def-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-arrows] [def-cbc-strict-tower-ordinary-proper-open-arrows]. For vertically stacked squares $Q_1$ above $Q_2$, with left proper maps $r_1,r_2$, right proper maps $p_1,p_2$ and middle open $i_1$, their intrinsic outer alpha satisfies
$$\alpha_{Q_2Q_1}=(\alpha_{Q_1}G_{r_2})\circ(G_{p_1}\alpha_{Q_2}).$$
For horizontal squares $Q_1$ left of $Q_2$, with top opens $k,l$, bottom opens $i,j$ and verticals $r,p,q$, it satisfies
$$\alpha_{Q_2Q_1}=(J_l\alpha_{Q_1})\circ(\alpha_{Q_2}J_i).$$
For any base change $h:T_1\to T$, let $a:W_1\to W$, $c:S_1\to S$, $d:V_1\to V$ be the projections and $Q_1$ the induced square. With $\theta:G_{p_1}G_h\cong G_aG_p$ the canonical square identification, one has
$$(\beta_kG_r)\circ(G_a\alpha_Q)\circ(\theta J_i)=(\alpha_{Q_1}G_c)\circ(G_{p_1}\beta_i).$$
Every formula inserts the canonical inverse-image and open-extension compositors. These equalities hold already for module sheaves, termwise on strict towers and complexes, and after exact localization in their unbounded derived categories. They identify the intrinsic outer clopen construction with the pasted one; no chosen factorization, finite-coefficient condition, cartesianness of the original squares, or faithfulness of derived evaluation is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the three module-sheaf component identities to every module M. Natural-transformation extensionality and the identity components of associators give the equations alphaVerticalPasted=alphaVerticalOuter, alphaHorizontalOuter=alphaHorizontalPasted, and alphaCubeOriginal=alphaCubeChanged.

Apply congrArg to mapHomologicalComplex, to whiskeringRight on inverse systems, and to their composite. This gives the complex, tower, and tower-complex equalities without any evaluation-faithfulness claim.

Encode each finite diagram as an ExactDerivedPasting.Expression over words of the exact tower functors. At every tower index, the ordinary evaluation is the appropriate module-sheaf component identity, so the two expressions have equal ordinary evaluation. Localization.natTrans_ext, the word factorization and expression_factors identify their derived evaluations. The intrinsic alpha cell is identified by alpha_eq_localized_singleAlpha, using uniqueness after Q and cancellation of invertible factorization maps. The gComp cell follows from its definition. The jComp and beta cells are identified using the proved jComp_fac and beta_fac; square cells use squareG_lift and exact square factorization. Thus all derived cells are the specified alpha, beta, squareG, gComp and jComp. Taking components of the equality of derived natural transformations gives exactly the final equation in each theorem. No derived evaluation is used to detect morphisms. The proved helper exactPasting_congr packages this localization congruence without an unnecessary finiteness assumption on the indexing type; its private component API normalizes the finite pasting trees.
